criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A new test dispatches a job on branch A, switches to branch B (which contains the base commit), finishes the job, and shows that B's tip is unchanged and the outcome is stale (or blocked) with a reason naming the dispatch branch.
criteria.evidence: I ran it here: `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_with_its_records_goes_stale` and `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_without_its_records_changes_nothing` both pass. In (a), the job is dispatched on main and verification switches to `other`. The outcome is Stale and its reason names `main` and `other`. `other` gains only paths under records/, the content fingerprint is unchanged, there is no greeting, and main's tip is unchanged. In (b), `other` lacks the job's records: `go` errors naming `main` and saying nothing was written, and `other`'s tip equals the tip before the job. This tip check applies only to case (b); in (a), `other` gains a records-only stale commit, which is within the criterion's 'stale' option. The land.rs unit test `a_job_dispatched_elsewhere_is_refused_on_another_branch` passes. It also shows the same call with `Dispatched::Unknown` returns `Plan::Tree`, so the test fails without the new check. The full suite is from the CI record.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows a job still lands as a fast-forward when the checked-out branch at finish is the dispatch branch, including the records-only-changes replay case.
criteria.evidence: Both tests pass here. `a_candidate_lands_over_a_records_only_interleave` now also asserts that `dispatch_branch` is `main`, that the current branch is main and that the greeting landed. `a_job_lands_when_the_dispatch_branch_is_checked_out` checks two cases: with head at the base it gets `Plan::Tree`, and after an excluded-path commit (the replay case) it gets a tree whose fingerprint matches and which keeps PRIVATE.md.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows the retry-after-blocked landing path (close.rs ~484) also refuses when the current branch differs from the dispatch branch.
criteria.evidence: This passes here. The job is blocked by a local edit. After switching to `other`, `go` errors with text containing `main` and 'stays blocked'. `other`'s tip is unchanged, there is no greeting and no outcome-landed.json. After checking out main, the retry lands. close.rs `retry_landing` matches `Plan::OtherBranch` and refuses, the same way it handles `Stale`.

findings.summary: A retry refused on the wrong branch gives misleading advice.
findings.evidence: For `OtherBranch` the error reuses the stale text: 'job {id} can no longer land: ... It stays blocked; `athena close {id} --why ...` abandons it, and a new ask redoes the work'. In fact the job lands once the dispatch branch is checked out, as the test and the CHANGELOG ('stays blocked until the dispatch branch is checked out again') say. A user who reads this error may abandon a job that could still land. Simpler fix: give `OtherBranch` its own message telling the user to check out the dispatch branch and run `go` again.

findings.summary: The two branches show the job differently after a wrong-branch finish.
findings.evidence: In case (a) the stale outcome is committed only on `other`. On the dispatch branch the job reads as `interrupted`, as the lifecycle test asserts, and `go` refuses it, so the user must run `athena retry`. This was planned and is tested, and the error and status give `retry` as the next step, but the job's state now depends on which branch is checked out.

findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: Neither file is on the expected deliverables list. Both are on the planned-files list and both are needed: lifecycle.rs holds the behavior tests for criteria 1–3, and run/mod.rs records `dispatch_branch` at dispatch. Neither adds unrequested behavior.

summary: The change does what was asked. A job now records the branch checked out when it is dispatched (`Job.dispatch_branch`, set in run/mod.rs). `land::plan` checks that branch before the ancestor rule, so both landing paths enforce it: the first landing (close.rs `land_or_block`) and the retry after a blocked landing. On another branch the job lands nothing. If that branch holds the job's records, the job goes stale with a reason naming both branches. If it does not, `go` fails without writing anything. A retry on another branch is refused and the job stays blocked. Detached HEADs are refused. Jobs dispatched before this change have no recorded branch and keep the old rule. I ran every planned demonstration in this snapshot and all passed: 2 wrong-branch lifecycle tests, 19 land.rs unit tests (including the new same-branch replay, other-branch, detached and check-order tests), the blocked-retry test, the records-only interleave test, and 66 records tests (including round-trips with and without the field). fmt, clippy and the full test suite are taken from the recorded CI run. There are no blocker or major findings. One error message gives misleading advice: a retry on the wrong branch says the job "can no longer land" and that "a new ask redoes the work", when checking out the dispatch branch is enough. Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list but were planned and are needed.
